school: Pragmatic 'keep what works' tuning: Getreuer's QMK tap-hold practice (Chordal Hold, scoped Flow Tap), Precondition's home-row-mods guide, r/ErgoMechKeyboards incrementalism, symbol placement from Rust frequency.
summary: This is a sound layout. It is QWERTY with a light set of home-row mods (no Shift on the index fingers), ':' unshifted on the home row (right for both Vim and Rust paths), and Space/Enter/Tab/Esc on the thumbs. So I keep every letter and thumb where it is and put the effort into firmware behaviour and the gaps. The worst problems are timing, not placement. The default quick-tap term turns ' {', ' &' and ' ->' (a space, then holding Space for a symbol) into a repeated space plus a letter, and does the same to Esc-then-Shift in Vim. With no permissive hold, a quick NAV chord can leak an Enter that sends a chat message. And switching on Flow Tap with its defaults would break snake_case, because it treats the Space thumb as a typing key. The functional gaps are no modifiers on NAV (so ⌥←, ⌘← and ⇧-selection are impossible), no F-keys anywhere, no ⌘-click on the mouse layer, mouse-layer KC_NO keys that silently eat the first letters typed after a click, and no reliable Shift+Enter. I fix these with mods on NAV in the same order as the base home-row mods, an FN tri-layer that mirrors the digits, a dedicated ⇧⏎, two Rust arrow macros and a Leader for the long tokens. Only eight existing keys change position.

layers.name: Base
changes: KEPT: every alpha, the ⌃⌥⌘ / ⌘⌥⌃ home-row mods with no Shift on F/J, ':' unshifted on the home-row pinky (right for Vim and for Rust '::' paths), ';' bottom-right, both Backspaces (the left one matters while your right hand is on the Navigator), both Tabs, and all four thumbs. This is muscle memory worth keeping.

Top row (was all KC_NO apart from Esc): Leader above T, Caps Word above Y, and ⌃⌘⇧4 (screenshot to the clipboard, for pasting into Slack or an LLM chat) top-right. These are rare, harmless keys, so an overshoot from Esc or Bspc costs nothing. In Oryx put a placeholder such as F24 on the Leader key and map it to leader_start() in process_record_user (C), so an Oryx re-export can't overwrite it.

Space/SYM thumb: quick-tap term set to 0 (C). With the default (200 ms), tapping Space and then holding it for a symbol repeats the space and types the base letter. That breaks ' {', ' &', ' ->', ' |x|', all very common in Rust (e.g. 'fn main() {' gives 'fn main()  j').
Esc/⇧ thumb: quick-tap term 0 (C). Today, Esc followed by holding the same thumb for Shift (Vim '<Esc>A', '<Esc>O') repeats Esc and types a lowercase a/o.

Enter/NAV and Tab/NUM thumbs: permissive hold on (C), so 'thumb down, tap J, thumb up' is ↓ and not 'Enter j'. That stray Enter is how a NAV chord sends a chat message today. The Enter thumb also gets a 175 ms tapping term: a hesitant press now sends nothing rather than Enter. Quick-tap is 0 on both.

Home-row mods: Chordal Hold (thumbs exempt), Flow Tap 150 ms and permissive hold (C). Opposite-hand shortcuts such as K+C → ⌘C fire on the nested release with no 200 ms wait. Mid-word rolls can no longer turn into mods. Same-hand chords still need the hold you use today.

Flow Tap is scoped to the home-row mods only (C). Its default treats the Space thumb as a typing key, which would force a space whenever you hold Space within 150 ms of a letter, so 'user_name' would come out as 'user hname'.

Key override: ⇧ + ';' sends '?' (C). ';' sits where '/' was on ANSI, so Shift+that key gives '?' exactly where your fingers expect it, which helps in chat. Nothing is lost, because ':' already has its own key.
Double-tap OSM⇧ turns on Caps Word (config.h), for SCREAMING_SNAKE consts and env vars. The top-row CW key is the visible fallback.

Shift+Enter: OSM⇧ then Enter already works and stays. Holding ⇧ on R-outer while tapping Enter becomes reliable once permissive hold is on. There is a new dedicated ⇧⏎ on SYM + R-inner thumb (see SYM).
layers.why: The base already does the hard things right, so moving letters or thumbs would buy you weeks of relearning for little gain. The real damage comes from the default tap-hold timing on the thumbs: it eats ' {' after a space, Esc-then-Shift in Vim, and lets a quick NAV chord turn into a sent message. The changes are almost all firmware behaviour, plus three rare keys on the empty top row.

layers.name: Numbers
changes: KP-, KP+, KP*, KP/ → plain -, +, *, / in the same positions. Keypad keycodes send different escape sequences when a terminal or Vim switches to application-keypad mode (you get stray 'Om'/'Ok' text or no-ops). The position is unchanged, only the keycode.
MyComputer (top-right) → no key. That consumer code does nothing on macOS.

KEPT: digits 1-0 along the home row, '%' '^' above 5/6, the extra '0' under N, and transparent ',' '.' '=' Bspc for decimals, ranges ('0..10') and arithmetic. All of this is good: Vim counts ('5j', ':42⏎') are thumb + home row.
While NUM is held, also holding the L-inner thumb (NAV) opens the new FN layer (tri-layer, C). Tapping L-inner still gives Enter, so ':42⏎' works without letting go of NUM.
F-keys deliberately not here: they live on FN in the same positions as the digits, so 'F2 is where 2 is'.
layers.why: This layer was already right ergonomically, with digits on the home row under a held thumb. The fix is the keypad keycodes, which misbehave in exactly the tools you use (terminal Vim, tmux). Nothing moves, so there is no relearning.

layers.name: Symbols
changes: '/' ↔ '\' swapped: '/' moves from the right-pinky top row to the right-pinky home row (the old '\' slot), and '\' goes up to P. '/' is the busiest symbol here for you: '//' and '///' doc comments in Rust, '/' search in Vim, paths and URLs in chat. '\' is close to unused in Rust. Same finger, one row, so it's cheap to relearn. On NUM, '/' stays on P next to - + *.

N: stray '0' (copied from NUM; nobody types 0 from the symbol layer) → '->' macro. M: empty → '=>' macro. Return types and match arms are on almost every screen of Rust. Both are now one key under the index finger, with no cross-hand '-' then '>' and no pinky trip to '='.

R-inner thumb (was transparent Tab/NUM) → ⇧⏎. Hold Space and tap the right inner thumb for a newline in Slack or an LLM chat. It is a plain key, so it fires on press. If you roll it too fast the result is Space+Tab, never a sent message.

KEPT: '_' on H (snake_case), '{' '}' on J K, '<' '>' on D F, '(' ')' on C V, '?' '&' '#' '|' '"' '!' '@' '[' ']' '`' '~' '$' '%' '^' '-' '+' '*'. These are already in good frequency order for Rust. Same-hand thumb+finger symbols are fine because the thumb moves independently, so I don't mirror the layer the way a minimalist would.
'::' deliberately not a macro: two taps on the home-row ':' are already as fast as one layer chord.
layers.why: Your symbol layer already puts Rust's heavy hitters (_ {} <> () & ?) on or near the home row, so I only fix two clear misallocations: '/' on a weak key while '\' wastes a home-row slot, and a stray '0'. I also add the two Rust tokens that really cost effort, plus a safe Shift+Enter. Nothing you type often moves except '/', and it moves one row on the same finger.

layers.name: Nav / IDE / media
changes: Left home row → plain ⌃ ⌥ ⌘ ⇧ on A S D F, the same order as the base home-row mods plus ⇧ on the index finger. Selection and jumps become one-handed chords: ⌥←/⌥→ by word, ⌘←/⌘→ to line start/end in Mac-native apps where Home/End only scroll, ⇧+arrows to select, ⌥⇧→ to select a word, ⌘⇧↑ to select to the top. Holding D and tapping the R-inner thumb gives ⌘Tab. Today none of this is possible, because ⌘/⌥ live under the arrows. Colour these four keys green like the base mods.

The three VS Code search keys displaced from the home row keep their columns and move up two rows: ⌃⇧G (Source Control) above S, ⌘⇧F (search in files) above D, ⌘⇧H (replace in files) above F. ⌘⇧E (Explorer) stays on G. This is the main relearn in the whole proposal.
Q (was empty) → ⌘. (Quick Fix: rust-analyzer imports, fill match arms). B (was empty) → ⌘⇧P (command palette).

Media Stop (top-right) → Del (forward delete), on the Backspace position so it reads 'Backspace, but forward'. Most macOS players ignore Stop, and a Mac has no forward delete without fn. ⌥ on S + Del deletes a word forward.

KEPT: vim arrows on HJKL with Home/PgDn/PgUp/End under them, ⌘\ split, ⌘⇧[ ] tab switching, ⌘↓, copy-path keys, the ⌘1/⌘2 tap dance, ⌃` terminal, ⌥Space launcher, Play, volume, Mute, ⌘⇧4. Those are your choices and they're good.

KEPT on Right Option: the tmux keys ⌥P/⌥H/⌥L/⌥N. If they work today, your terminal already treats Right Option as Meta. If you ever switch terminals and they print '˙' or 'π', change the four keycodes to LALT.
R-inner thumb held while NAV is held → FN layer (tri-layer, C).
layers.why: The single biggest functional gap in the layout is that NAV has arrows but no modifiers, which is crippling for editing text in Slack or an LLM chat box. Putting the mods where your fingers already expect ⌃⌥⌘ fixes it with almost no learning. Every existing VS Code and tmux shortcut survives, and three of them shift up in their own columns.

layers.name: Mouse
layers.activation: automouse: move the Navigator (750 ms timeout); LLock pins it
changes: Every unused key: KC_NO → transparent. In this firmware's auto-mouse code, KC_NO is on the 'skip' list. A letter you type within 750 ms of a click is silently eaten, and the layer stays on and eats the next one too. Transparent keys type normally and end the layer, so 'click the chat box, start typing' just works.

⌘/⌥/⌃-click: hold the normal home-row mod (D, S, A), which now shows through. Auto-mouse ignores a mod-tap while it is held, so the layer stays up for the click. Chordal Hold allows it because the buttons are on the other hand. Use ⌘-click for go to definition and links in new tabs, and ⌥-click for VS Code multi-cursor. I did not use plain mods here: they would swallow an 'a', 's' or 'd' typed right after a click.
Left outer home key (OSM⇧ position) → a plain held ⇧, for Shift-click range selection and Shift-drag. A one-shot can't be held through a click or drag.

LLock (was C) and CPI-/CPI+ (were V/B, same columns) move to the top row. That frees Z X C V, so D(⌘)+Z/X/C/V gives undo/cut/copy/paste without leaving the pointer. These are rare keys, and the top row is never hit by accident while typing.
KEPT: BTN1/BTN3/BTN2 on Y U I, drag-scroll on F, toggle-scroll on G, and the 750 ms timeout.
layers.why: Most mouse-layer pain today comes from KC_NO: lost keystrokes after every click, and no modifiers. Making the layer transparent fixes both at once and reuses the home-row mods you already know. The click and scroll keys you use stay exactly where they are.

layers.name: FN / system
layers.activation: hold both inner thumbs (Enter/NAV + Tab/NUM): tri-layer (C)
changes: NEW. F1-F10 sit exactly where 1-0 are on NUM. F11 and F12 take the two outer home keys. VS Code: F2 rename (S), F12 go to definition (right outer), F8 next problem (K), F5 start/continue debug (G), F9 breakpoint (L), F10 step over, F11 step into.
Bottom row = the shifted F-key above it: ⇧F5 stop debugging, ⇧F8 previous problem, ⇧F11 step out, ⇧F12 find references. Both thumbs are busy here, so the shifted versions need their own keys.
System corner keys you need rarely and must never hit by accident: Boot (bootloader, for flashing) top-left, Lock (⌃⌘Q, lock screen) top-right, RGB on/off and LED brightness on the left.
Build it as layer 5 in Oryx (it exports the keys and LEDs). The only custom C is the activation, update_tri_layer_state(state, 1, 3, 5).
layers.why: The layout had no F-keys at all, and they are the fastest route to rename, go to definition, next problem and the debugger in VS Code. A tri-layer keeps them on the home row under both thumbs, numbered exactly like your digits, without stealing a key or a thumb from anything else.

combos.keys: L-outer + L-inner thumbs (Space + Enter), pressed together
combos.why: Optional one-motion newline: roll the left thumb flat across both keys, so Enter alone sends and the 'fat' press makes a newline. If it fires by accident (a trailing space rolled into Enter) you get a newline, never a send. I add no combos on letter keys: with home-row mods, Chordal Hold and Flow Tap already in play, alpha combos are the next misfire source (for example ',+.' would fire on 'e.g.,'). Oryx supports thumb combos. Use COMBO_TERM 40.

macros.why: SYM + N. On almost every fn signature and closure return type. It replaces a cross-hand '-' (U) then '>' (F).
SYM + M. On every match arm. It replaces a pinky stretch to '=' followed by '>'.

macros.label: Lead m
macros.why: The most common Rust token that isn't a single symbol. (C)

macros.label: Lead s
macros.why: Nine characters for a mutating method signature. (C)

macros.label: Lead d
macros.why: 23 characters, typed on most struct/enum definitions. Edit it to your usual derive set. (C)

macros.label: Lead e
macros.why: Lands you ready to type the message. Works with or without editor auto-pairs, because VS Code and nvim-autopairs type over the auto-inserted closers. (C)

macros.label: Lead o
macros.why: Four shifted bracket chords on SYM become one sequence. (C)

macros.label: Lead p
macros.why: Debug printing. 20 characters, a third of them shifted symbols. (C)

features.name: Tap-hold baseline (config.h)
features.why: This keeps today's 200 ms feel and switches on the per-key callbacks below. Leave RETRO_TAPPING and HOLD_ON_OTHER_KEY_PRESS off: either one would make the Enter thumb fire (or turn into NAV) in situations where it doesn't today. Don't also set per-key tapping terms in Oryx, or the callbacks will be defined twice.

features.name: Per-key tap-hold callbacks (C)
features.why: Each line removes one misfire this user hits daily. ' {' and ' &' after a space; Esc→⇧ in Vim; 'Enter j' from a quick NAV chord. It also makes opposite-hand ⌘/⌃ shortcuts fire without waiting out the 200 ms.

features.name: Chordal Hold, thumbs exempt (C)
features.why: A same-hand roll on a home-row mod (D then C mid-word) settles as letters immediately. The thumbs must be '*': Chordal Hold settles a same-hand press as a tap on the spot, which would otherwise break Space + left-hand symbols, NUM + right-hand digits and the FN tri-layer. The ':'/⌃ key (DUAL_FUNC_0 is really LT(3, KC_X)) is covered automatically.

features.name: Flow Tap on home-row mods only (C)
features.why: A home-row mod pressed within 150 ms of a letter is always a letter, which removes fast-typing mod misfires. The default get_flow_tap_term also applies to LT(2, KC_SPACE) because its tap is KC_SPC. That would force a space whenever you hold Space within 150 ms of a letter, so snake_case and 'foo(' would break. Hence the explicit scope. It already turns itself off while ⌘/⌃/⌥ is held.

features.name: Key override ⇧; → ? (C)
features.why: This puts '?' back on Shift + the key right of '.', where every ANSI typist looks for it. That matters in chat. The ':' key and SEND_STRING macros are unaffected, because neither goes through KC_SCLN key events.

features.name: Caps Word on double-tap Shift
features.why: This works with your OSM(MOD_LSFT). Caps Word is already compiled in (keyboard.json) but had no trigger. Use it for SCREAMING_SNAKE consts, statics and env vars. '_' keeps it going, so MAX_RETRY_COUNT is one go.

features.name: Leader with instant single-key sequences (C)
features.why: This is Vim-style <leader> for the long Rust tokens, without spending prime keys on them. leader_add_user returning true fires on the first key, so there is no timeout lag. Leader resolves home-row mod-taps to their letters, so 's' and 'd' work. Any other key after Lead (Esc, say) just cancels.

features.name: FN tri-layer (C)
features.why: Holding both inner thumbs (you never hold them together for anything else today) opens F-keys on the home row. Layer 5 fits under LAYER_STATE_8BIT and sits above the automouse layer 4. Define the layer's keys and colours in Oryx. This function is the only code.

missing: F-keys: there were none anywhere. Now F1-F12 plus ⇧F5/⇧F8/⇧F11/⇧F12 on FN, numbered like your digits.
Modifiers on NAV: ⌥←/⌥→ word jumps, ⌘←/⌘→ line ends, ⇧-selection and ⌘Tab were impossible.
Modifier-clicks on the mouse layer: ⌘-click (go to definition, open link in a new tab), ⌥-click (multi-cursor) and ⇧-click (range select).
Keystrokes typed right after a click were silently eaten by KC_NO on the mouse layer.
A dedicated, send-proof Shift+Enter (SYM + R-inner thumb, plus an optional thumb combo).
Tap-hold safety config: no Chordal Hold, Flow Tap, permissive hold or quick-tap tuning, so ' {' after a space, Esc→⇧ in Vim and quick NAV chords misfired.
A Caps Word trigger, though Caps Word is already compiled in.
Rust token shortcuts: '->' and '=>' keys, Leader snippets for &mut, derive, test, cfg(test), unwrap, expect, Ok(()), println!.
VS Code Quick Fix (⌘.) and the command palette (⌘⇧P) on NAV.
'?' on Shift + the old '/' key (ANSI position).
Screenshot to the clipboard (⌃⌘⇧4) for pasting into chats.
risks: Chordal Hold does not make same-hand shortcuts faster. D(⌘)+C still needs the >200 ms hold you use today. Opposite-hand ones (K+C, K+V, K+Z, ':'-key+C for ⌃C) become instant, so lean on those.

Permissive hold on the home-row mods leaves one residual misfire. Start a word slowly after a pause of more than 150 ms with a lingering pinky ('a' still down while 'n' goes down and up) and you get ⌃N. Flow Tap only covers mid-word rolls. If it bites, return false from get_permissive_hold for A and the ':' key only.

The Space thumb deliberately gets no permissive hold and no Flow Tap. '_' and the other symbols still need Space held a moment before you release the symbol key, as today. The win is that ' {', ' &' and ' ->' right after a space now work every time.
Quick-tap 0 on the thumbs removes hold-to-repeat for Space, Enter, Tab and Esc. Backspace is a plain key and still repeats.

Enter has a 175 ms tapping term, so a slow, hesitant Enter sends nothing. That is the point, but you may notice it for a day. One stray-Enter path remains: a very fast roll where the thumb comes up before the arrow key. If it still happens, enable hold-on-other-key-press for that one key, at the cost of Enter-then-letter rolls in code turning into NAV.
NAV relearn: ⌃⇧G, ⌘⇧F and ⌘⇧H move up two rows. Expect about a week of reaching for the home row.
The '/' ↔ '\' swap breaks the mirror between SYM's and NUM's operator rows. On NUM, '/' stays on P.

Mouse layer: typing right after a click now types, but y, u and i are still mouse buttons for 750 ms. A tap on the left outer key there is a plain Shift, so a capital typed straight after a click can come out lowercase.
Leader snippets run as commands if you fire them in Vim normal mode. Use them in insert mode only.

Several pieces are custom C (tap-hold callbacks, chordal layout, Flow Tap scope, key override, Leader, tri-layer). They live outside the Oryx keymap array, so re-exports merge cleanly, but a change in Oryx to the same keycodes (for example renaming DUAL_FUNC_0) needs a matching edit.
macOS maps F11 to Show Desktop. Turn that off (System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Mission Control) to get VS Code step-into back.
The optional Space+Enter thumb combo depends on how comfortably your thumb covers both keys. If it feels awkward, skip it, because SYM + R-inner already gives ⇧⏎.
